concepts.name: Origins and Background of the Khilafat Movement
key_dimensions: Role of Ottoman Caliphate's defeat in WWI as the trigger
Treaty of Sèvres (1920) and its provisions dismembering Ottoman Empire
Pan-Islamic sentiments among Indian Muslims and their connection to the Caliph
Distinction between Khilafat as a religious institution vs. political mobilization tool

concepts.name: All India Khilafat Committee: Formation and Structure
key_dimensions: Founded in 1919 — exact year and key founders (Maulana Mohammad Ali, Shaukat Ali, Maulana Azad)
Central vs. provincial committee structure and coordination with INC
Khilafat Conference of 1919 vs. 1920 — key resolutions and differences
UPSC trap: Distinction between All India Muslim League and All India Khilafat Committee leadership overlap

concepts.name: Gandhi's Decision to Support the Khilafat Movement
key_dimensions: Gandhi's strategic calculation: Hindu-Muslim unity as prerequisite for Swaraj
Gandhi's role as leader of Khilafat deputation to Viceroy (1920)
Criticism from contemporaries (Jinnah, Tagore) against Gandhi's religiously-framed politics
UPSC trap: Gandhi supported Khilafat despite it being a purely Islamic religious cause — his reasoning vs. his secular credentials

concepts.name: Linkage Between Khilafat Movement and Non-Cooperation Movement
key_dimensions: Formal merger at Calcutta Special Session (September 1920) and Nagpur Session (December 1920)
Khilafat as one of the two grievances (alongside Punjab wrongs/Jallianwala) for launching NCM
Joint programme: boycott of councils, courts, schools, foreign cloth
UPSC trap: NCM was launched PRIMARILY for two issues — Khilafat + Punjab wrongs, NOT solely for Swaraj

concepts.name: Ali Brothers (Mohammad Ali and Shaukat Ali): Role and Significance
key_dimensions: Their internment during WWI (1916–1919) and its radicalizing effect
Mohammad Ali's Comrade and Hamdard newspapers as propaganda tools
Their eventual estrangement from Gandhi and INC post-1924
UPSC trap: Mohammad Ali Jauhar (Khilafat leader) vs. Mohammad Ali (later PM of Pakistan) — two different persons

concepts.name: Hijrat Movement (1920): An offshoot of Khilafat
key_dimensions: Theological basis: India declared Dar-ul-Harb (land of enemy), migration to Afghanistan as religious duty
Scale: Approximately 18,000–20,000 Muslims migrated; Afghanistan's refusal and tragic consequences
Relationship with Khilafat Committee — endorsed but not officially organized by it
UPSC trap: Hijrat is frequently confused as part of NCM; it was a separate, parallel movement

concepts.name: Moplah Rebellion (Malabar, 1921): Causes and Consequences
key_dimensions: Dual character: Agrarian resentment (Hindu landlords vs. Muslim tenants) + Khilafat religious fervor
Declaration of Khilafat Kingdom in Malabar and its short-lived existence
British suppression and the infamous 'Wagon Tragedy' (1921)
UPSC trap: Impact on Hindu-Muslim unity — Gandhi initially defended Moplahs, later condemned violence; this is a frequently tested contradiction

concepts.name: Khilafat Movement and the Question of Violence vs. Non-Violence
key_dimensions: Internal tension between mass Islamic mobilization and Gandhian non-violence principle
Chauri Chaura (1922) as the event that exposed this fault line
Gandhi's unilateral suspension of NCM — Khilafat leaders' (Ali Brothers') opposition to this decision
UPSC trap: Gandhi suspended NCM, NOT Khilafat Movement — they were technically separate; Ali Brothers continued agitation

concepts.name: Abolition of the Caliphate by Mustafa Kemal Ataturk (1924)
key_dimensions: Turkish Grand National Assembly's formal abolition of Caliphate on March 3, 1924
Immediate collapse of the ideological basis of the Khilafat Movement in India
Indian Muslim leaders' response — Aga Khan's proposal for a new Caliphate
UPSC trap: The movement died due to EXTERNAL factor (Turkish abolition), not British suppression — important analytical distinction

concepts.name: Khilafat Movement's Impact on Hindu-Muslim Relations
key_dimensions: Short-term: Unprecedented Hindu-Muslim unity (1919–1922), communal harmony
Long-term: Post-1922 communal riots (Kohat riots 1924, Calcutta riots 1926) — reversal of unity
Debate among historians: Did Khilafat movement strengthen or ultimately damage Hindu-Muslim unity?
UPSC trap: UPSC often asks about 'consequences' — the movement's failure accelerated communalization of politics

concepts.name: Role of Maulana Abul Kalam Azad in the Khilafat Movement
key_dimensions: His Al-Hilal and Al-Balagh newspapers as ideological platforms pre-Khilafat
Theological argument: Indian Muslims' obligation to Caliph and opposition to British
His position within Khilafat Committee vs. his simultaneous role in INC
UPSC trap: Azad's stance differed from Ali Brothers — he emphasized composite nationalism more consistently

concepts.name: British Government's Response to the Khilafat Movement
key_dimensions: Montagu's assurances to Muslim delegation and subsequent betrayal via Treaty of Sèvres
Policy of divide and rule — encouraging moderate Muslims (Aga Khan, Muslim League)
Repressive measures: arrests of Ali Brothers, use of sedition laws
UPSC trap: British simultaneously negotiated Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (1919) while betraying Khilafat promises — dual policy

concepts.name: Khilafat Delegations and Diplomatic Efforts
key_dimensions: Khilafat deputation to British PM Lloyd George (1920) — Gandhi's participation
Representation at Paris Peace Conference — Indian Muslim delegation's failure
Internal debate on whether to pursue constitutional or extra-constitutional methods
UPSC trap: Gandhi's support for Khilafat deputation preceded formal launch of NCM — chronological sequence matters

concepts.name: Tanzim and Tabligh vs. Shuddhi and Sangathan Movements: Post-Khilafat Reactions
key_dimensions: Hindu revivalist Shuddhi (reconversion) and Sangathan (Hindu unity) movements as reaction
Muslim response through Tanzim (organization) and Tabligh (proselytization)
Role of Swami Shraddhanand and his assassination (1926) in escalating tensions
UPSC trap: These movements are a DIRECT consequence of Khilafat's failure — cause-effect linkage frequently tested

concepts.name: Khilafat Movement and the Emergence of Separatist Politics
key_dimensions: How failure of Khilafat emboldened Muslim League's separatist narrative post-1924
Jinnah's consistent opposition to Khilafat as mixing religion with politics
Revival of Muslim League under separate electorate demands after Khilafat's collapse
UPSC trap: Jinnah LEFT INC in 1920 partly over NCM/Khilafat — this is a key turning point toward Pakistan movement

concepts.name: Economic Dimensions of the Khilafat-NCM Programme
key_dimensions: Boycott of foreign cloth — its specific impact on Muslim merchant communities
Swadeshi as a common platform between Hindu and Muslim participants
Tilak Swaraj Fund (raised ₹1 crore) — Khilafat Committee's parallel fundraising
UPSC trap: Economic boycott was more successful than institutional boycott — differential success rates

concepts.name: Historiographical Debates on the Khilafat Movement
key_dimensions: Nationalist interpretation (Nehru): Genuine Hindu-Muslim unity movement
Revisionist view (Mushirul Hasan): Movement strengthened communal identity over national
Marxist view: Class contradictions within Muslim participation ignored by religious leadership
UPSC trap: 'Was Khilafat a nationalist or communalist movement?' — UPSC Mains frequently tests nuanced evaluation

concepts.name: Khilafat Movement and Women's Participation
key_dimensions: Muslim women's participation in picketing and processions — break from purdah tradition
Bi Amma (mother of Ali Brothers) as a symbolic figure of mobilization
Comparison with women's participation in parallel NCM activities
UPSC trap: Women's role in Khilafat is less discussed but significant — UPSC uses this to test depth of preparation

concepts.name: Press and Propaganda in the Khilafat Movement
key_dimensions: Mohammad Ali's Comrade (English) and Hamdard (Urdu) as primary organs
Maulana Azad's Al-Hilal and Al-Balagh — pre-movement ideological groundwork
British censorship under Press Act and its counter-effect of radicalizing opinion
UPSC trap: Distinction between pre-Khilafat press (Azad) and Khilafat-period press (Ali Brothers) — chronological accuracy

concepts.name: Legacy and Long-term Significance of the Khilafat Movement
key_dimensions: First mass movement that brought together Hindu-Muslim masses under one platform
Demonstrated Gandhi's ability to mobilize across religious lines — and its limitations
Paradox: Movement meant to foster unity ultimately sharpened communal identities
UPSC trap: Khilafat is often romanticized as a unity movement — but its FAILURE and consequences are equally, if not more, important for examination
